foundations.title: Five-minute governed-agent demonstration
foundations.summary: Run the same research-agent plan with and without a Nornyx-derived egress control.
foundations.why_it_matters: A beginner can see the entire problem, intervention, evidence, and limitation before learning the vocabulary in depth.
outcomes: Distinguish an assistant message from an agent side effect
State a precise cooperative-enforcement claim and limitation

foundations.title: Models, software, and responsibility boundaries
foundations.summary: See how probabilistic model output differs from deterministic application code and where reliability controls belong.
foundations.why_it_matters: Governance cannot be designed honestly until model, provider, application, framework, tool, and operator responsibilities are separated.
outcomes: Explain an LLM in plain language
Contrast variable output with deterministic code
Place validation and authorization in the application boundary

foundations.title: Prompts, context, and structured outputs
foundations.summary: Compose a prompt and context stack, label authority and taint, then validate model-shaped data before use.
foundations.why_it_matters: Retrieved data and operator instructions can arrive together, while malformed structured output can turn uncertainty into a software failure.
outcomes: Validate structured output before application use

foundations.title: Assistants, tools, and side effects
foundations.summary: Connect and disconnect tools to see when a model proposal becomes an observable business effect.
foundations.why_it_matters: Function calling creates reachability; it does not create authorization, safety, or evidence by itself.
outcomes: Trace a tool call from proposal to effect
Use counters instead of refusal text for side-effect claims

foundations.title: How agents run
foundations.summary: Explore plans, workflows, loops, memory, retries, handoffs, parallel work, and framework responsibilities on one timeline.
foundations.why_it_matters: Governance requests and evidence identities must survive the execution patterns that agent frameworks actually introduce.
outcomes: Separate model, framework, application, and governance roles

foundations.title: Engineering reliable AI applications
foundations.summary: Repair an evaluation suite covering variable output, schema drift, prompt injection, unauthorized tools, timeouts, retries, and missing telemetry.
foundations.why_it_matters: AI quality is established through invariants, evaluations, observability, bounded failure handling, and ordinary secure software delivery.
outcomes: Test invariant behavior instead of exact prose
Recognize hidden skips and silent fallback

00.summary: Watch retrieved text steer a susceptible planner and measure what changes when tools are attached.
00.why_it_matters: A bad plan is only a sentence until reachable tools turn it into an effect.

01.summary: Find contradictions across four control artifacts and generate coordinated controls from one checked contract.
01.why_it_matters: Independent instructions drift; an authoritative checked source makes disagreement visible.

02.summary: Decompose governance claims into declaration, decision, enforcement, evidence binding, and assurance.
02.why_it_matters: Integrity, completeness, runtime use, and prevention are different propositions with different evidence.

03.summary: Wire the same decision as PDP-only, enforced, and bypassed, then compare the resulting effects.
03.why_it_matters: A correct policy decision prevents nothing unless an unavoidable enforcement point applies it.

04.summary: Resolve framework identities, assign capabilities, and inspect delegation and handoff authority on a graph.
04.why_it_matters: Framework names and reachable functions are not governance identities or delegated authority.

05.summary: Run the same prompt-injected research plan across an ungoverned path and a gated trust-zone boundary.
05.why_it_matters: The planner can remain fooled while an enforced boundary prevents the resulting external effect.
05.migration_classification: preserve behind service API and adapt

06.summary: Produce allow, deny, and approval-required decisions while varying explicit request and time inputs.
06.why_it_matters: Total, default-deny, deterministic evaluation makes decisions reproducible and missing authority explicit.

07.summary: Trace effective controls to profiles and modules, then attempt permitted narrowing and forbidden widening.
07.why_it_matters: Composition without provenance or monotonic restrictions can silently weaken superior policy.

08.summary: Mutate approval actor, role, action, evidence, revision, time, and grant fields and observe exact refusals.
08.why_it_matters: Approval is a bounded, attributable assertion—not a boolean, model message, or permanent unlock.

09.summary: Break the decision service and compare fail-open, fail-closed, and explicitly bounded degraded behavior.
09.why_it_matters: Evaluator failure semantics determine whether an incident becomes an outage or an unauthorized effect.
09.migration_classification: preserve behind service API and adapt

10.summary: Build and validate a contract- and revision-bound event stream, then remove required bindings.
10.why_it_matters: Logs are observations; governance evidence needs identity, sequence, producer, decision, and artifact bindings.

11.summary: Tamper with generated content and event order inside an isolated workspace, then restore verification.
11.why_it_matters: Digests and locks expose drift, while occurrence and sequence rules expose replay and duplication.

12.summary: Assign assurance per surface and correct claims that outrun their evidence, producer, or enforcement boundary.
12.why_it_matters: Assurance tiers attach to a named mechanism and surface—not to an entire system by association.

13.summary: Compare a governed wrapper with a direct bypass and build a machine-readable coverage inventory.
13.why_it_matters: A correct wrapper covers only paths that invoke it; a negative control must prove the alternate route exists.
13.migration_classification: preserve behind service API and adapt

14.summary: Repair a real staged `.nyx` contract through synchronized visual, source, generated-control, and diagnostic views.
14.why_it_matters: Beginners can author the authoritative contract without creating an incompatible visual-only format.

15.summary: Separate profile provenance from network-artifact locking and break each binding in an isolated copy.
15.why_it_matters: Locks answer exact content questions; they do not prove correctness, authorization, or runtime use.

16.summary: Load one lock-verified immutable Authorizer, inspect detached state, and exercise its typed request interface.
16.why_it_matters: A single assured interpretation prevents split-brain policy decisions across components.

17.summary: Distinguish missions, operations, occurrences, and attempts, then drive a deterministic artifact drift gate.
17.why_it_matters: Retries, repeated work, duplicates, replay, and resume require identities that survive framework execution.

18.summary: Run real pinned CrewAI synchronous tool calls through the Nornyx adapter and inspect exact coverage.
18.why_it_matters: Adapter enforcement is cooperative and surface-specific; unsupported and unwrapped paths remain explicit.
18.migration_classification: preserve behind service API and adapt

19.summary: Execute real LangGraph denial, retry, loop, parallel, interrupt, and resume variants with occurrence-aware evidence.
19.why_it_matters: The original linear graph did not execute the framework behaviors its lesson promised.

20.summary: Run adapter conformance, examine independent-enforcement requirements, and scan an inert suspicious package.
20.why_it_matters: Static declarations, runtime conformance, external enforcement, and package evidence support different claims.

21.summary: Move a contract change through visual check, review, generation, lock, evidence, test, conformance, and publish gates.
21.why_it_matters: A delivery pipeline must fail on the right defect and must never turn missing checks into green assurance.

22.summary: Run a new executable Forge multi-agent delivery network with distinct author, reviewer, release, and human roles.
22.why_it_matters: The original lab described Forge and multi-agent separation of duties without executing the end-to-end workflow.

23.summary: Build threat, residual-risk, interpretive standards-mapping, claim-register, and audit-package records from actual runs.
23.why_it_matters: The original placeholder mapping and raw-authorizer evidence could not support its named adapter or compliance claims.

24.summary: Design, run, break, validate, and defend a learner-authored Northstar multi-agent workflow as the capstone.
24.why_it_matters: The original scripted walkthrough did not require learner design, real framework execution, or a defensible assurance review.
